<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a04e9d76c13363280bdd86950603f0e0e6deb6dd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8bc61d3c4441a47e00f16cd7618b793393878bdb` — the merge of head `1dfad411f3605ce8d35b358524e1ec6393bc5d67` into base `a04e9d76c13363280bdd86950603f0e0e6deb6dd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8bc61d3c4441a47e00f16cd7618b793393878bdb && git checkout 8bc61d3c4441a47e00f16cd7618b793393878bdb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a04e9d76c13363280bdd86950603f0e0e6deb6dd 1dfad411f3605ce8d35b358524e1ec6393bc5d67 && git checkout -B drift-repro a04e9d76c13363280bdd86950603f0e0e6deb6dd && git merge --no-ff 1dfad411f3605ce8d35b358524e1ec6393bc5d67

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a04e9d76c13363280bdd86950603f0e0e6deb6dd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a04e9d76c13363280bdd86950603f0e0e6deb6dd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1dfad411f3605ce8d35b358524e1ec6393bc5d67`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.validation-type-mismatch-refused.ts, packages/formula/src/expression-refusal.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-validate-expression.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts, packages/objectql/src/publish-type-mismatch-fail-closed.test.ts + packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts (`firstTypeMismatch`, `UNSOUND_OVERLOAD_RE`, `coercionFor`, `NUMERIC_STRING_RE`), packages/formula/src/expression-refusal-codes.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`checkPredicate`, `checkConditional`, `evaluateValidationRules` requiredWhen arm, `isReadonlyWhenLocked`, `evaluateOptionVisibility`, the severity loop), packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts (`wrapDeclarativeHook` condition gate), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (formula reads null), packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.ts (`NullGuardOutcome`, surface ledger), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`saveMetaItem`, `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules`), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset) + published spec path. Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `@objectstack/formula` `ExprSchemaHint.faultOutcome?: 'fail-closed'`: new optional key on an exported interface; absent reproduces the previous call byte for byte. Additive, minor. **Right.**
2. `ExpressionRefusalParams['type-mismatch'].outcome?: 'fail-closed'`: new optional param, present exactly when the error arm fires. **Right as a type change**; see ④-A.
3. Accept-set narrowing at the author-time gate: `type-mismatch` moves from `warnings[]` to `errors[]` at fail-closed sites, reaching `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint`, the active object save door and `publishPackageDrafts` (`assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` 422); draft saves stay ungated (#4463 D1). Sites: validation `condition` / `when` and every nested predicate, field `requiredWhen` / `readonlyWhen`, option `visibleWhen`, hook `condition` (single-object and `targets`). **Right**, each verified against its evaluator in ④.
4. Not narrowed: formula `expression` (reads null), flow conditions, field `visibleWhen` / `settledWhen`, field-group and action predicates, `conditionalFormatting`, sharing rules (compiled to a filter). **Right.**
5. `@objectstack/mcp` `validate_expression`: `site: 'validation'` now answers what publish answers; other sites untouched. **Right**, carried by the BREAKING changeset.
6. `@objectstack/spec`: one new semantic D3 entry, id matches filename, shape matches `SemanticMigration`, no index edited (registry generated from the directory). **Right.**
7. No spec zod schema, protocol schema or `skills/**` change. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`formula`, `lint`, `mcp`, `spec` all `minor`; `fix(lint)!:` summary; `**BREAKING**` banner; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` identical on PR body and changeset; disposition `adr-0087: registered validation-type-mismatch-refused` with a FROM → TO section (a FROM → TO line contradicts `not-required`, so `registered` + a D3 entry is the honest disposition; precedent #28944). objectql gets only a test file, correctly not bumped. Check Changeset (runs the ADR-0087 registration gate), Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, dispatch-gates lint, Dogfood Regression Gate and Spec property liveness: success at record time; Build/Test families still in progress, none red.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev open question (flow conditions carry the false "evaluates to null" warning):** confirmed on the tree; `validate-null-guards.ts` documents that surface as `run-fails`. **Follow-up card, filed and linked on #29904 before the queue, not this PR**: the twin treats flows as a distinct outcome with its own wording, grading it error widens the narrowing beyond write-refusing roles, and the author sees a failed run rather than a bricked object.
2. **Advisory-severity validation rules** (`severity: 'warning' | 'info'`): an unevaluable advisory rule is logged, not refused (#24782), so the error text's "the write … is refused" is false for them, yet the gate refuses them. The nullable twin does the same. Accepted for parity; should-fix candidate for the same follow-up card.
3. `readonlyWhen` and option `visibleWhen` are not twin-covered; including them is correct (both refuse on a fault since ADR-0137 D2; this verdict prescribes no `has()`, so #4953 clause 3 does not bind).
4. Assignee/review steps and the signed trailer are harness matters, not reviewed here.

### ④ Design judgment

**Card scenario.** `record.name > 5` on a required text field in `validations[].condition`: on `main` a warning advisory, then every write 400; at the head `check(…, FAIL_CLOSED)` → error → publish refused at `objects[N].validations[0].condition`. The new objectql door test drives the real `saveMetaItem` + `publishPackageDrafts` and pins refused / formula-still-published / twin-unchanged.

**One decision, one place.** Role→severity is decided only in lint's `FAIL_CLOSED` ledger (nine `check()` call sites), with the MCP site map as the one declared mirror; the formula validator never guesses the site.

**Per file:** `validate.ts` holds (error arm after `date-arith`, before the warning return; message claims match `coercionFor` / `NUMERIC_STRING_RE`); `validate-expressions.ts` holds (every ledger row verified against its evaluator; display-only predicates left at warning); its tests retire exactly the behaviour the card retires and add per-site, formula, display and twin controls; MCP files hold (other sites' hints byte-identical); the objectql door test holds; the D3 entry holds (nit B).

**FROM → TO in this CEL dialect:** `size(record.name) > 5` ✓, `double(record.name) > 5` ✓ (faults on non-numeric text, as the message says), `record.active == true` ✓ (equality excluded from `UNSOUND_OVERLOAD_RE`).

**False positives probed:** number/currency/percent/select/lookup/autonumber are `dyn`, so a mismatch fires only on declared text/boolean/date fields. The one accepted false positive, a text field always holding numeric text, is the card's ask, follows the twin's precedent, and the message names the rewrite.

**Findings:**
- **A (should-fix):** `expression-refusal.ts`'s contract ("a code names ONE message template") and `expression-refusal-codes.test.ts`'s pins are strained: `type-mismatch` now has a second template chosen by `params.outcome`, and `'fail-closed'` is not a substring of its message. CI is green because `SWEEP_SCHEMAS` carries no `faultOutcome`; no consumer keys on the code today. Fix in the follow-up (pin the case, or give the arm its own code).
- **B (should-fix, nit):** the D3 entry's `acceptanceCriteria` says a create "answers 200"; the data door answers 201.
- **C (should-fix → follow-up card):** ③-1 and ③-2.

No must-fix. The narrowing takes away no declared capability: everything it refuses already refused every write at runtime (or, for numeric text, is named with its exact rewrite), and it makes the spec's own fail-closed refusal real at author time.
